view: Revision 2. Emerging consensus (six-member simple mean): 2w 32 up / 30 range / 38 down, this_quarter 33/34/33, next_quarter 42/26/33; TB2 'recommend fired' (narrative) with five members deferring; today's bar a 'candidate climax, unconfirmed'. I attack it on both points. (a) TB2 should be ruled FIRED on the rule text, but as a buying policy, not as a second bearish input to the forecast, and it needs a written un-pause test now. (b) Calling today a climax low is not supportable: the bar is open, the low came from a news gap rather than exhausted selling, the market is calm, and two binary events (print 2026-11-17, testimony before 2026-11-25) can retest 148.80. On 2w I am slightly less bearish than the consensus (the shock is in the price; the remaining events are two-sided); on the quarters I sit near the consensus with a fatter down tail.

probabilities.defs: 2w ±5%, quarters ±10%, vs price_at_call 164.33 (2026-11-12 intraday, revision 2). next_2_weeks: up = close > 172.55, down = close < 156.11, range between, measured at the 2026-11-25 close (2026-11-26 is Thanksgiving, market closed). this_quarter: to the last close of 2026-12-31; next_quarter: to the last close of 2027-03-31; up > 180.76, down < 147.90, range between. up + range + down = 100.

evidence.point: Outside view 33/45/22 (n=258). I move to 34/29/37: range -16 because daily ATR is 6.0% and today's own range (148.80-167.14) is wider than the whole ±5% band; down +15 for trend, testimony and the TB1 path; up +1 because the CEO exit itself is now in the price and the print is two-sided. The consensus raised down by 12-18 in every seat for the same headline; part of that is availability (the vivid gap), since price_at_call 164.33 already includes the reaction.

Outside view 39/43/18 (n=253). I move to 32/33/35 (down +17). The down line 147.90 is 1.1 below today's low 148.80, so a single failed retest resolves it; up needs 180.76, i.e. entry into the 179.92-185.22 gap and a reclaim of the 100W SMA 175.09 under an interim CEO, a CEO search and FOMC/CPI on 2026-12-09/10.

Outside view 50/31/19 (n=247), from a 2021-2026 sample with no founder-CEO exit and inside NVDA's bull regime (price still +32.9% over the 200W SMA). The window to 2027-03-31 is about 20 weeks, so range should be below 31. I move to 40/25/35: founder loss and open DOJ/Congress tracks are regime risk the base rate does not contain.

(a) TB2 - the strongest NOT-FIRED case, stated fairly: the 8-K gives no reason; there is no charge against Huang and no finding against Nvidia; the board probe is framed as whether Huang was a target of a foreign intelligence operation (victim framing); the DOJ inquiry is about Megaspeed's routing, not Huang; he agreed to testify (cooperation, not compulsion in the slice); a senator's resignation call is political, not legal or regulatory. On this reading the exit could be reputational or personal.

(a) TB2 - why I still rule FIRED: TB1 was drafted with an explicit evidentiary bar ('government finding, charge, settlement or company admission'); TB2 was not. Its trigger is a departure 'under legal or regulatory pressure', and the facts at the moment of departure are exactly that: resignation from CEO and the board effective immediately, no succession plan, no stated reason, three days after a Wachtell Lipton board investigation opened, during a DOJ inquiry and a public resignation call, followed by congressional testimony. Requiring proof of motive would add a condition the owner did not write. Pre-commitment rules exist to bind on days like this; reinterpreting one the day it triggers is the System-1 failure the Kahneman card warns about.

(a) TB2 - attack on how the consensus is handling it: (1) five of six members deferred 'to the chair', so the recommendation rests on one member's read; the chair should rule on the text, not on a vote. (2) Several members raise their down buckets for 'possible TB2' and fundamentals proposes another +5 down if it is ruled fired: the ruling is a buying policy and adds no new price information; the governance facts are one evidence group and must not be counted again through the ruling. (3) The rules define no un-pause condition. Without one written now, the pause either becomes indefinite or gets argued away on the first rally (narrative's own pre-mortem and sentiment's FOMO note point at that risk).

(b) Climax low - first objection: the bar is open ('hammer/spring shape is unconfirmed until the close'). The lessons log (2026-11-11) already caught one call made on an open bar. Price 164.33 is below today's high 167.14 and 5.4% below the prior close 173.73: as of now it is a red day with a long lower wick, not a reversal close.

(b) Climax low - second objection: the low was produced by an overnight news gap (open 151.005, -13.1%; low 148.80, -14.3%), not by a sequence of exhausted selling into a final flush. A recovery from a news-gap open is common when the news is a single, known event; it shows the market re-priced the headline, not that sellers are exhausted. Exact timing of the low within the day is not in slice.

(b) Climax low - third objection: 3.8x volume is the fourth heavy day in a row (Mon 462.7M, Tue 429.3M, Wed 339.2M, today 498.56M so far). Persistent heavy volume through a -19.7% two-week drop is as consistent with a holder-base change (distribution to new owners) as with a single climax. Volume cannot tell them apart; only follow-through can.

(b) Climax low - fourth objection: there is no market-wide washout. VIX 17.62, indices reversed higher and AMD/Broadcom rose up to about 5% on the news (news_governance). Capitulation logic (forced sellers exhausted) fits a market panic; this is a single-name information event, which resolves on information (testimony, guidance, CEO search), not on seller exhaustion.

(b) Climax low - fifth objection: two binary events sit right after the candidate low: the print 2026-11-17 under an interim CEO who is also CFO, and Huang's testimony before 2026-11-26, plus monthly opex 2026-11-20. A low printed before two scheduled shocks cannot be called until both have passed without a close below 148.80.

(b) Climax low - sixth objection: options positioning failed. The intraday recovery may be short covering, put monetisation or dealer hedging into the 2026-11-20 expiry, which often fades, rather than real buying. This unread page is exactly the one the 'climax' call depends on. Sentiment pages are stale too (AAII week ending 2026-11-04, CNN partial).

(b) The strongest bull case, stated fairly: the condition now applies (two_week_change_pct -19.7%) and history says 2w 50 up / 50 range / 0 down and 13w 4 of 4 up (median +32.1%); today recovered 10.4% off the low on 3.8x volume; fundamentals for the quarter just ended were earned before the exit; CFO continuity helps the print. But n=4 in overlapping weekly windows is perhaps one to three independent episodes, none with a CEO exit. Near-zero weight; I use it only to keep 2w up at 34.

My revision-1 point still stands and the news strengthens it: NVDA/SOX ratio -44.4% over 52w (27.9202 -> 15.5182) and -14.4% over 13w; AMD +169.15% YTD and AMD/Broadcom rallied on the resignation. The market reads the exit as a share/mindshare question, not only a governance one; that does not fade with the headlines.

Derived (approximate, from slice numbers): next-quarter EPS 2.47 on revenue 108.67B implies a net margin near 55% vs 63.7% TTM, and next-FY EPS 9.29 is below 4 x 2.47 = 9.88. Estimates already embed margin compression; the ~17.7x forward P/E at 164.33 is 'cheap' only if estimates survive an interim-CEO guide. FCF fell 48.59B -> 21.40B and debt rose 12.81B -> 38.86B, causes not in slice. Analyst targets (avg 309.21, low 180) predate the exit and are one lagging group: not a level.

what_would_change_my_mind: FASTEST CHECK 1 - today's close (2026-11-12) and the weekly close (2026-11-13): a close above 167.14 today with the weekly bar closing above 164.27 and the long lower wick intact would make the climax reading credible; I would move 2w to about 38 up / 32 down. A close below 154.53 on either day means the reversal failed; 2w down to about 42 and this_quarter down to about 40.

FASTEST CHECK 2 - no daily close below 148.80 through the 2026-11-18 close (post-print) and through Huang's testimony (before 2026-11-25): surviving both binary events is the only real confirmation of a low. A close below 148.80 puts this_quarter down above 45 and L3 (141-145) in play.

FASTEST CHECK 3 - the reason for the exit, from the 2026-11-17 release/10-Q legal-proceedings and risk-factor language and from the testimony before 2026-11-25: any link to Megaspeed/DOJ confirms TB2 and raises TB1 odds; a stated personal reason unrelated to the probe, plus a board statement, would meet the un-pause test I propose and move next_quarter up about 5. Secondary on the same dates: NVDA/SOX ratio vs 15.5182 in the week ending 2026-11-20.
Thesis breaks: a DOJ charge, settlement or company admission (TB1) or an enacted export restriction (TB3) would override everything above.
notes_for_chair: TB2 RULING (red team): FIRED, on the rule text. TB1 carries an explicit proof bar and TB2 does not; the departure happened under live legal and regulatory pressure (board investigation, DOJ inquiry, public resignation call, congressional testimony) with no stated reason. Owner confirms. Rule it on the text, not on today's price action in either direction.

Proposed un-pause test for the owner to approve before the next run (so the pause is neither indefinite nor rationalised away): all of (1) a stated reason for the exit unrelated to legal/regulatory matters, from a filing, board statement or the testimony; (2) no Nvidia-specific legal-proceedings disclosure on Megaspeed/DOJ in the 2026-11-17 release or 10-Q; (3) TB1 and TB3 not fired. Re-check after the testimony (before 2026-11-25).

Do not double count: the CEO exit is one governance evidence group. It is already in price_at_call and in every member's down bucket; the TB2 ruling is a buying policy and must not add another down adjustment (fundamentals proposes +5 if fired).

Climax low: label today 'news-gap reversal, unconfirmed', not 'capitulation'. Minimum confirmation = check 1 plus check 2. The lessons log already contains one open-bar error; a 10.4% intraday recovery is the most tempting setup for a second.

Pre-mortem for my view: if badly wrong in three months, the likely reason is that the exit removed the legal overhang from the company, the print was clean under Kress, and 148.80 was the low; then my down tails and the TB2 pause cost entries near the bottom. The un-pause test is the remedy, not a looser TB2 reading.

Price_at_call 164.33 is again a streaming intraday print in the middle of a 148.80-167.14 day; today's close may differ by several percent, so the 2w buckets are measured from a non-close. Log the close alongside the call.
